findings.title: 75-80% of S/4HANA projects derailed by change-management failure
findings.desc: Poor planning, communication, and stakeholder engagement -- not technology -- are cited as the leading cause of failed SAP transformations.
findings.fix: Run a formal change-management workstream from the blueprint phase, not as an afterthought.

findings.title: Hypercare period after go-live is a high-risk control gap
findings.desc: Elevated access and rapid troubleshooting right after cutover can quietly break security and compliance controls if unmanaged.
findings.fix: Define hypercare governance and access-control rules before go-live; loop in auditors early.

findings.title: A petabyte of forgotten 27-year-old EDI data surfaced mid-migration
findings.desc: Long-lived legacy environments often hide undocumented data volumes that only appear once a migration is underway.
findings.fix: Run a comprehensive data-discovery and readiness assessment before committing to a timeline or budget.

findings.title: Only 37 of 200 surveyed companies had finished their S/4HANA migration
findings.desc: Most respondents were still mid-transformation, and more than six in ten had already exceeded their planned migration budget.
findings.fix: Build budget contingency in from the start and tighten IT/business alignment on priorities before kickoff.

findings.title: Uncontrolled scope changes without governance derail migrations
findings.desc: Scope changes are normal during a migration, but without a structured approval process they accumulate into major cost and schedule risk.
findings.fix: Stand up a Change Advisory Board with a prioritized backlog so scope changes are evaluated, not just absorbed.

findings.title: Incomplete data migration leaves gaps that surface after go-live
findings.desc: Missing or mismapped data during cloud data-transfer steps causes downstream problems that are expensive to trace back.
findings.fix: Define explicit source-to-target data mapping and dedicated migration-script testing before cutover.

findings.title: In-house teams often lack the specialized skills cloud SAP migrations require
findings.desc: SAP-on-cloud migrations need expertise that generalist IT teams frequently do not have in-house.
findings.fix: Engage SAP-certified managed-service partners and run parallel internal upskilling so knowledge transfers in-house.

findings.title: Teams lose track of what has been tested, turning migration risk into guesswork
findings.desc: Without centralized test visibility, teams do not know what is validated and what is still at risk heading into go-live.
findings.fix: Centralize test management so coverage and open risks are visible across the whole program.

findings.title: Every custom integration point is a potential failure during cutover
findings.desc: The more heavily customized and connected a SAP environment is, the higher the risk that cutover breaks something downstream.
findings.fix: Inventory every custom integration point ahead of time and test each one during phased cutover rehearsals.

findings.title: Standardized Fiori UX feels like a downgrade, driving user resistance
findings.desc: Users accustomed to years of custom screens often resist SAP standard interfaces, undermining an otherwise technically successful migration.
findings.fix: Pair UI rollout with targeted training and clear messaging on productivity gains.

findings.title: Shrinking ABAP talent pool inflates cost and timelines
findings.desc: Original customization developers have often retired or moved on, leaving organizations short on skills right when they are most needed.
findings.fix: Start ABAP/SAP-skills succession planning early, and budget for contractor rates that reflect real scarcity.

findings.title: Inconsistent master data causes failed billing after go-live
findings.desc: Duplicate or conflicting customer, vendor, and material records cause load errors during conversion and billing problems afterward.
findings.fix: Run a dedicated data-cleansing and validation phase before cutover.

findings.title: Skipping experienced help on landing-zone design creates endless security rework
findings.desc: Trying to force existing datacenter architecture into a hyperscalers model leads to prolonged security back-and-forth.
findings.fix: Bring in someone who has done this before and design the landing zone deliberately from a small pilot.

findings.title: Cloud adopted as just a virtualization provider reproduces old problems
findings.desc: Migrating without organizational change means teams end up running the same operational problems on someone elses infrastructure.
findings.fix: Treat the migration as an operating-model change, not a lift-and-shift.

findings.title: Misconfigured IAM script deleted live patient records with no recoverable backup
findings.desc: A rushed cloud migration without immutable backups or versioning led to permanent data loss and an unassessable compliance exposure.
findings.fix: Enable immutable backups and versioning before any migration script runs.

findings.title: Ungoverned multi-cloud strategy duplicated services and spiked costs
findings.desc: Independent teams managing AWS, Azure, and GCP without shared governance led to duplicated spend and outages that were nearly impossible to troubleshoot.
findings.fix: Put a centralized cloud governance and FinOps function in place before splitting workloads across providers.

findings.title: DIY cloud migration without expertise led to a ransomware attack
findings.desc: A team that migrated without outside help made network-design errors and exposed endpoints, which were later exploited.
findings.fix: Even small teams should get a security review of network and IAM design before go-live.

findings.title: A single product migration took three attempts across three years
findings.desc: Disentangling a codebase and moving from VMs to containers proved so complex that only a dedicated team and phased plan finally succeeded.
findings.fix: For complex migrations, staff a dedicated team with a hard deadline and a phased approach.

findings.title: Cost blowouts pushed some companies to repatriate workloads out of the cloud
findings.desc: Some organizations that migrated to the cloud later moved workloads back to owned infrastructure to cut costs, saving tens of millions.
findings.fix: Periodically re-evaluate cloud vs owned-infrastructure economics at scale.

findings.title: 84% of system integration projects fail or partially fail
findings.desc: Underestimated legacy complexity, inadequate testing, and unclear objectives repeatedly derail integration initiatives across industries.
findings.fix: Treat integration as its own project with dedicated testing and scoping.

findings.title: The average enterprise has only 29% of its applications connected
findings.desc: Disconnected systems create information silos that limit visibility, slow decisions, and block further modernization.
findings.fix: Adopt an incremental API-led or iPaaS integration layer rather than attempting full connectivity in one project.

findings.title: Unpatched legacy software is IT teams top security concern
findings.desc: Legacy platforms that no longer receive patches or updates create security exposure that grows the longer modernization is delayed.
findings.fix: Prioritize modernization of the systems carrying the highest security exposure first.

findings.title: Most leaders say their data is not ready for AI agents because of integration debt
findings.desc: Years of accumulated legacy integration debt is now blocking the data foundation that AI initiatives depend on.
findings.fix: Fund data-foundation modernization as its own initiative before launching AI programs on top of it.

findings.title: Integration failures cost Global 2000 companies an estimated $400B a year
findings.desc: Downtime from integration failures is expensive at scale -- most mid/large enterprises report hourly downtime costs well into six figures.
findings.fix: Invest in redundancy, staged rollouts, and tested rollback plans proportional to the real cost of downtime.
